title: Bonding and Inlet Screen Change for the Centre Tank Boost Pump Canisters
abstract: Improved electrical bonding path and a coarser inlet screen for the centre tank boost pump canisters, closing a fuel system safety finding on bonding resistance and reducing nuisance low-pressure warnings from screen blockage.

sections.reason: A fuel system safety review found that the bonding resistance between the centre tank boost pump canister and the tank structure exceeded the design limit on a significant proportion of the in-service fleet, with 62 of 210 sampled aircraft measuring above ten milliohms. The cause was corrosion of the canister mounting flange under the original sealant. Separately, operators reported nuisance low fuel pressure warnings during centre tank transfer, traced to partial blockage of the fine inlet screen by sealant debris left from earlier tank entry work.
sections.description: Each centre tank boost pump canister is fitted with a dedicated bonding lead terminated on the tank structure with self-locking nuts EN968165-23, replacing the reliance on the mounting flange contact. The mounting clamp D2820008967217 is renewed and its faying surface is left unsealed and bare within a controlled area to guarantee the bonding path. The fine inlet screen is replaced by a coarser item carried on the restrictor housing D2820003250655, whose mesh passes debris up to 0.8 millimetres while retaining the particle size the pump requires. The screen retention nuts AGS15973-37 are changed to a captive type so that they cannot be lost inside the tank. The pump FINs 732QT8 and 7953QT are unaffected as line replaceable units, and the distribution pump FIN 5QA keeps its existing rating. Work is done through the tank access panels in zones 531, 631 and 114. Drawings D28201157245 issue F and D28200071626 issue G carry the bonding and screen detail.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 0.9 kg per aircraft, negligible balance effect. No electrical load change; bonding resistance is brought below five milliohms at every canister. The canister assembly is one-way interchangeable because the new bonding lead needs a structure terminal that the pre-modification tank does not have. Nuisance low-pressure warnings during centre tank transfer fell by 78 per cent in the trial fleet. AMM tank entry and pump removal tasks for ATA 28-20 were amended, and the periodic bonding resistance check introduced by the safety review is deleted for post-modification aircraft.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in on the production line at MSN Z09424 in September 2017 and available for retrofit by a single bulletin. Retrofit requires tank entry and purge, about four days including the ventilation periods, and is normally combined with a scheduled tank inspection.

type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN Z09424, absorbed in the centre tank build station
